prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1145; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's policyholder reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection, with the claimant seated in the passenger vehicle. Coverage was verified and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Police report obtained; responding officer confirms the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene and documents the impact location consistent with the insured's description.

Entry 3: Recorded statement taken from the other driver, who independently describes the same sequence of events and the vehicle positions at impact.

Entry 4: Photographs of both vehicles reviewed. Damage to the front bumper, hood and airbag deployment pattern appears consistent with the reported impact speed and direction.

Entry 5: Two independent witnesses interviewed by phone; both confirm the accident occurred as described and that the claimant was in the passenger seat.

Entry 6: Repair estimate and vehicle history checked. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy inception.

Entry 7: Claimant's representing attorney submitted a demand package listing a concussion diagnosis following the collision. The reported injury is consistent with the mechanism and force of the crash.

Entry 8: Medical records reviewed. Treatment followed a typical course, with frequent visits early on that tapered as symptoms improved. Records also note a minor strain to the same area many years ago that resolved fully.

Entry 9: Claimant's account has remained the same across every conversation, including the initial call, the written statement and the attorney-led interview.

Entry 10: Medical review notes the prior strain healed completely and does not appear to account for the current symptoms or treatment pattern.

Entry 11: File reviewed and assessed as consistent across accident facts, damage, witness accounts and medical course. Proceeding with evaluation of the bodily injury claim under counsel's representation.
